title: The C51 projection and the quantile Huber loss
brief: Project shifted return distributions back onto a fixed support and check that the projection keeps mass and mean, train the result with cross-entropy, then fit quantiles with QR-DQN's asymmetric loss.
hints: In c51_project, compute tz = clip(r + gamma * (1 - term) * z, v_min, v_max) and b = (tz - v_min) / dz for all atoms at once, with shape (B, N). Then l = floor(b) and u = ceil(b).
When b is an integer, l == u and both shares p * (u - b) and p * (b - l) are zero. Either nudge l down or u up by one in that case, or add p * (l == u) to atom l.
np.add.at(m, (rows, l), p * (u - b)) accumulates into repeated indices correctly. Plain m[rows, l] += ... drops repeats.
c51_loss is -(m * torch.log_softmax(logits, dim=1)).sum(dim=1).mean(). Its gradient with respect to the logits is (softmax - m) / B.
In quantile_huber_loss build u = target[:, None, :] - pred[:, :, None], shape (B, N, M), so the prediction index i sits on axis 1 and pairs with taus[i].
